text: Transactions and receipts carry their own accounting. But a lot of what happens to a balance afterward isn't a transaction or a receipt at all, it's an adjustment, a write-off, a late charge. Receivables activities give each of those a default GL account so nobody picks one from scratch.

A receivables activity is a small setup record: a name, an activity type, and a default account, or an AutoAccounting reference instead of a fixed one. When someone performs the related action, entering an adjustment, writing off a receipt, recording miscellaneous cash, they pick one of these activities and its defaults drive the accounting.

Here are the main types. Adjustment, required, every implementation needs at least one before anyone can adjust a balance. Miscellaneous cash, for money received that isn't a payment against a transaction, like a rebate. Late charges, for overdue-transaction charges. Receipt write-offs, for small remaining balances. Credit card chargeback and refund. And earned versus unearned discount, so a correctly-taken discount and a late one post to different accounts.

Picture Northwind Fixtures Co with an AR Adjustments Bad Debt activity pointed at a bad-debt expense account, and an Early Payment Discount activity pointed at a contra-revenue account. A twenty-five dollar rounding difference gets adjusted off using the first one, posting straight to bad debt. Harborline Retail Group correctly takes its two percent discount on a ten thousand dollar invoice, and that two hundred dollars posts automatically through the Earned Discount activity.
